name: Universal Tennis Rating
summary: UTR is a match-result rating run by UTR Sports that places every tennis player on one scale from 1.00 to 16.50, whatever their age or gender, with a separate UTR Pickleball Rating (UTR-P) on a 1.0 to 10.0 scale. The tennis rating is a weighted average of up to 30 recent match ratings from the last 12 months, and moves according to the share of games won against what the algorithm expected. Basic ratings are free.

operatorFact.text: UTR Sports (Universal Tennis), founded by its chairman and chief executive Mark Leschly

scale.text: Tennis: 1.00 to 16.50, higher is stronger. Pickleball (UTR-P): 1.0 to 10.0, beginner to expert or professional
scale.citation: FAQs; UTR-P figures from How UTR Pickleball Rating works

basis.text: Calculated daily from match results using a modified Elo method: each match gets a match rating and weight, and the rating is the weighted average of up to 30 matches from the last 12 months. Games won count in tennis; UTR-P counts points won
basis.citation: FAQs: How is the UTR Rating calculated?

formats.text: Pickleball: separate singles and doubles ratings; doubles partners are not averaged
formats.citation: FAQs: Is the UTR-P Rating for singles or doubles?

launched.editorNote: Year UTR launched not stated on utrsports.net pages opened (UTR-P page says 'over a decade of experience').

cost.text: Free for players: the operator says it has no plans to charge for ratings
cost.citation: FAQs: How does the UTR-P Rating compare to the UTPR

name: ITF World Tennis Number
summary: The World Tennis Number is the International Tennis Federation's global rating, giving each player a number from 40 (lowest) down to 1 (highest) on one scale for all ages and genders. It is calculated from match results analysed set by set, comparing the actual score with the algorithm's prediction, and players get separate singles and doubles numbers. National bodies including the LTA and USTA use it for seeding, selection and finding evenly matched opponents.

operatorFact.text: Developed by the International Tennis Federation and adopted by national associations, including the USTA, in over 170 countries

scale.text: 40 (lowest) to 1 (highest); shown to one decimal place in the UK

basis.text: An Elo-style calculation from match results, analysed at set level: the pre-match numbers predict the outcome and each number moves by how the actual score compares. New adults start from a player questionnaire

formats.text: Both: separate singles and doubles numbers

launched.text: Introduced in Britain by the LTA in October 2021, among the first countries

cost.text: Free in Britain for LTA Advantage members in the Play or Compete categories

name: National Tennis Rating Program
summary: NTRP is the USTA's rating for adult players in the United States, running from 1.5 for a beginner to 7.0 for a touring professional in half-point steps. Players can self-rate against written descriptions of each level, and USTA League play then produces computer ratings, which compare each match outcome with the outcome expected from the players' dynamic ratings. It was developed in 1978.

basis.text: Self-rated against written level descriptions, then computer-rated from USTA League adult division results (and in some sections sanctioned tournaments): the algorithm compares each match outcome with the outcome expected from the dynamic ratings of the player, partner and opponents
basis.citation: How does the year-end NTRP calculation work?

formats.editorNote: USTA pages opened mention partners (doubles) but do not state singles and doubles explicitly.

cost.text: Self-rating needs a free USTA account

name: Leistungsklasse (DTB performance class)
summary: The Leistungsklasse (LK) is the German Tennis Federation's level system, with 25 steps where LK 1 is the best and LK 25 the lowest, shown to one decimal place. Each win in a qualifying match improves the winner's LK by an amount that depends on the gap between the two players, while the loser's LK is unchanged; a small weekly addition drifts every LK back towards 25 unless the player keeps winning. Singles, doubles and mixed results count.

scale.text: 25 steps, LK 1 best and LK 25 lowest, with one decimal place; values are capped at 1.5 and 25.0

basis.text: Wins in matches of two winning sets improve the winner's LK by points based on the LK gap, divided by a hurdle value and weighted for age group and scoring format; the loser's LK is unchanged. Every LK rises by 0.025 a week (up to 25), and results are processed weekly

formats.text: Singles, doubles and mixed; doubles use the partners' average

launched.editorNote: Year the LK system was introduced not stated in the 2024 regulations.

cost.editorNote: Cost not stated in the regulations; new players are registered by their regional association (§ 10).

name: KNLTB playing strength and rating
summary: In the Netherlands every KNLTB club member gets a playing strength (speelsterkte), a whole number from 1 to 9 where beginners start at 9, plus a more precise rating for singles and for doubles. The rating, set by the Dynamic Playing Strength System (DSS), moves after every match by an amount based on both players' ratings and the result, and feeds the following season's playing strength. The KNLTB also runs ratings for padel.

scale.text: Playing strength: a whole number from 1 to 9, with beginners at 9; a separate decimal rating sits beneath it

basis.text: Every match changes the rating: wins raise it and losses lower it, by up to 0.275 a match depending on both sides' ratings; doubles use the pair's average. Playing strength for the next season is set from the rating
basis.citation: Hoe wordt mijn rating bepaald?; FAQ

formats.text: Both: separate playing strength and rating for singles and doubles

launched.editorNote: Launch year of DSS not stated (page says the algorithm was tested on 2018 and 2019 match data). A new padel rating model started on 1 January 2025.

cost.text: Given to every player who joins a KNLTB club or buys a Spelerspas (player pass)

name: Dynamic Universal Pickleball Rating
summary: DUPR is a pickleball rating run by DUPR Inc. that places players on a scale from 2.000 to 8.000, with new players shown as NR (not rated). Ratings update after every shared result, based on how a player or team performed against the score expected from everyone's ratings, with verified club, league and tournament matches weighted more than self-posted ones. Players get separate singles, gender doubles and mixed doubles ratings.

operatorFact.text: DUPR Inc., based in Delray Beach, Florida

scale.text: 2.000 to 8.000, higher is stronger (2 Novice, 3 Intermediate, 4 Advanced, 5 to 8 Professional); new players start as NR
scale.citation: FAQs: What is the DUPR rating scale?

basis.text: From match results: performance against the expected score, weighted by match type (verified matches count more than self-posted ones) and recency. Doubles use the average of the partners' ratings as a team rating

formats.text: Separate ratings for singles, gender doubles and mixed doubles, plus age-group ratings for players aged 50 to 65 and over

launched.editorNote: Launch year not stated on dupr.com pages opened.

cost.text: A paid DUPR+ membership adds brand discounts, tournament access and an ad-free app

name: Playtomic level
summary: The Playtomic level is the player rating inside the Playtomic court-booking app, widely used to match padel players of similar standard in open matches. It runs from 0 to 7, with 7 the highest, and moves with match results and the strength of the opponents.

basis.text: Calculated from match results and opponents' levels; it rises and falls as players win or lose

formats.editorNote: Format handling not stated on the blog; Playtomic help centre (playerhelp.playtomic.com) returned 403.

name: SquashLevels
summary: SquashLevels is a squash rating run by squashLevels Ltd and endorsed by World Squash and the PSA as the official world squash ratings. It gives every player a dynamic level after each match, set by performance against expectation, taking account of opponent strength and the full match score, so points won count even in defeat. National federations including Squash New Zealand use it in place of older grading systems. A basic rating is free; extra statistics need a paid plan.

operatorFact.text: squashLevels Ltd; the official world squash ratings partner of World Squash (WSF) and the PSA

scale.editorNote: Scale not stated on pages opened; player examples on the home page range from 800 to 5,700.
scale.text: An open number, higher is stronger

basis.text: Calculated after every match from performance relative to expectation, taking account of opponent strength and the full match score

launched.editorNote: Launch year not found. Squash New Zealand adopted it early in 2024 (source-squashlevels-squash-nz).

cost.text: Free basic account with player rating and rankings; Gold £35 a year (£3.99 a month) and Platinum £45 a year (£4.99 a month) add history and statistics

name: Universal Squash Rating
summary: The Universal Squash Rating is US Squash's player rating, ranging roughly from 1.5 for a beginner to 7.0 for a top professional. It updates daily from every match entered in the Club Locker system, adjusting each player's rating by how the result compares with the expected outcome and weighting recent matches more. A player needs at least one win and one loss on record to get a rating.

operatorFact.text: US Squash, through its Club Locker system

basis.text: Updated daily from all matches recorded in Club Locker: each result is compared with the expected outcome, recent matches weigh more, and at least one win and one loss are needed for a rating

formats.editorNote: Not stated on the ratings page (US Squash also runs doubles).

launched.text: Algorithm developed for Club Locker and US Squash between 2012 and 2014 by Elder Research

cost.editorNote: Not stated on the ratings page.

name: USA Table Tennis rating
summary: The USATT rating is USA Table Tennis's official rating for players in sanctioned table tennis tournaments in the United States. Points are exchanged between winner and loser according to a ratings points exchange chart. It has covered singles only; USATT has announced official doubles ratings, plus separate hardbat and sandpaper ratings, from the 2026 US Open in December 2026.

operatorFact.text: USA Table Tennis (USATT), the national governing body in the United States

scale.editorNote: No range published on the pages opened; usatt.org/usatt-ratings did not render without JavaScript.

basis.text: Ratings points are exchanged after each match using USATT's points exchange chart, from results of USATT-sanctioned tournaments

formats.text: Singles; official doubles ratings start with the 2026 US Open (16 to 21 December 2026), held per player and starting at the singles rating

name: Ratings Central
summary: Ratings Central is an online table tennis rating system open to any club, league or tournament, and is the official rating of more than 20 national, state and regional associations. It uses probability and statistics to estimate each player's playing strength from results, and uses one scale for table tennis, hardbat and sandpaper play. Event directors pay a pay-what-you-think-is-fair fee.

operatorFact.text: Ratings Central, run by David J. Marcus and Sean P. O'Neill

scale.text: A points number with no published range, higher is stronger; the operator describes standards such as a 1500 or 2000 player. It is not the same scale as USATT's

basis.text: A statistical model: each player has an estimated playing strength, and the chance of an upset depends on the difference in strengths; results from tournaments, league and club matches are submitted by event directors

formats.editorNote: Not stated on the pages opened.

cost.text: Not free: event directors pay what they think is fair each year they submit events

name: Table Tennis England rating
summary: Table Tennis England publishes national rankings and ratings for players in its competitions, with monthly lists for men and women in cadet, junior, senior and veteran age groups. The system is Elo-based and head-to-head, weighted by tier of event, with bonus points for high finishes in tournaments; the ranking lists cover England-eligible players, while the rating lists include everyone competing in its events.

scale.editorNote: Scale not stated on the rankings page.

basis.text: Elo-based head-to-head system with weightings for event tier and bonus points for higher tournament finishes; refreshed each season (1 August to 31 July)

formats.editorNote: Separate lists exist by gender and age group; singles/doubles treatment not stated.

launched.editorNote: Launch year not stated; archive lists date back to 2014.

cost.editorNote: Not stated; public lists only name current Table Tennis England members.

name: Platform Tennis Index
summary: The Platform Tennis Index is the American Platform Tennis Association's performance rating for platform tennis, built by APTA volunteers from match data. Like a golf handicap, lower is better: most players fall between 0 and 100, the league average is in the 50 to 60 range, and the best players reach 0 or below. A PTI improves with each set won and worsens with each set lost, by an amount that depends on the score and the relative strength of the teams.

scale.text: Generally 0 to 100, lower is better; new players are often 80 or more, top national players 0 or below, and a negative rating is possible

basis.text: Calculated from match results set by set, using the set score and the relative strength of the teams; start ratings come from a league default, a pro or captain, or early results, and are adjusted automatically if early results suggest they were wrong
basis.citation: How do PTIs adjust?; How do players get an initial PTI?

formats.text: Doubles: adjustments use the relative strength of the two teams

launched.editorNote: Launch year not stated; the page mentions a PTI 2.0 overhaul two seasons before an August 2026 update.

cost.editorNote: Not stated on the PTI page.
